answer: Make names, not money, the scarce input. Every key needs a named guarantor, jointly liable, capped at three keys, never itself guaranteed, so a thousand clones trace to hundreds of names. One upheld fraud claim voids the whole book of three, paying the claimant from the guarantor's seasoned balance and barring it from vouching. Signers stake a name plus four times the covered value in aged balance: a wall no cash climbs, since the limit is three, not a price. Honest work needs one signature, clear as quartz. Under that gale clones are no cheap seeds: a field of yarrow is counted by its stems.
